data.text:
Every scenario holds. I wrote `{"findings": []}` to `openspec/changes/249-rust-plan-new/.run/validator/findings.json`. I only read the code, tests and specs; I ran no build or test.

Note that the scenarios' "tests the change added or changed" list said none, but the patch does add and update tests. Those tests are the ones I judged against:

| Scenario | Code | Test |
|---|---|---|
| Plan argument errors | `next::arguments` | `tests/plan_next.rs::plan_argument_errors` (all 6 rows; checks it is a `Usage` error, the command and the message) |
| Refused next items | `select::failures` / `failure_message` / `choose`; `queue::read_state` with the `plan` command | `plan_next.rs::refused_next_items` (all 8 rows; also checks that no new folder is written) |
| Chosen next items | `select::choose`, `--replan` in either order | `plan_next.rs::chosen_next_items` (all 4 rows) |
| Next change numbers | `next/number.rs` | `plan_folder.rs::next_change_numbers` (all 5 rows) |
| Seeded proposal lines | `files::proposal` | `plan_folder.rs::seeded_proposal_lines` (all 4 rows) |
| Brief dates | `date::utc_date`, `files::brief` | `plan_folder.rs::brief_dates` (all 8 times; compares the whole brief) |
| Brief date from the system clock | `PlanFeature::new()` reads the system clock | `plan_folder.rs::brief_date_from_the_system_clock` |
| Handoff text | `next/handoff.rs` | `plan_folder.rs::handoff_text` (all 3 rows, including the folder case) |
| Prompt sections | `next/prompt.rs` | `tests/prompt_sections.rs::prompt_sections` (all 4 rows) |
| Golden change folder | the whole flow | `tests/golden_folder.rs` (compares every file byte for byte, plus the handoff with `<root>` replaced) |
| Plan feature commands | `feature.rs` | `plan_feature.rs::plan_feature_commands` (both commands, in order) |
| Queue argument errors | `feature.rs` | `plan_feature.rs::queue_argument_errors` |

None of these is a `passes_without_change` case:
- **New behavior:** the tests call `PlanFeature::new()`/`at()` and the `plan` command, none of which exist on the base, so none of them could pass there.
- **Queue argument errors:** the base already behaved this way for all three rows, including `planx`, so this is not new behavior.

One small gap, which I didn't count as a finding: in the third "Refused next items" row (the one with several failures), the test writes no `queue.md`, but the scenario says the default queue is there. The test is actually stricter this way. If the code read the queue before checking failures, it would fail with "Queue file not found" instead of the expected message, so the test still checks the scenario's result.
